subject: C
topic: Popular Names of J&K Personalities & Achievements

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah is popularly known by which title?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah was called 'Sher-e-Kashmir' (Lion of Kashmir) for his bold leadership in the freedom struggle and his role in shaping J&K's political destiny. 'Baba-e-Kashmir' is wrong — no such title is associated with him. 'Bulbul-e-Kashmir' is wrong — this title is not linked to Sheikh Abdullah. 'Shams-e-Kashmir' is wrong — this is not his popular name.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Habba Khatoon:

(i) She is known as the 'Nightingale of Kashmir'.
(ii) She was a 16th-century Kashmiri poet.
(iii) Her poetry is in the Kashmiri language.
(iv) She was the wife of the last independent ruler of Kashmir, Yusuf Shah Chak.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Habba Khatoon is called the 'Nightingale of Kashmir' for her lyrical poetry. (ii) is correct — she lived in the 16th century during the Chak dynasty period. (iii) is correct — her verses are in Kashmiri, expressing love and longing. (iv) is correct — she was married to Yusuf Shah Chak, the last independent ruler of Kashmir before Mughal conquest. All four statements are correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Father of Modern Kashmir' for his role in reforming and modernizing the state?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah is considered the 'Father of Modern Kashmir' for his land reforms (abolishing landlordism), educational initiatives, and efforts to establish democratic governance. Maharaja Ranbir Singh is wrong — he was a 19th-century Dogra ruler who promoted education but is not given this specific title. Maharaja Hari Singh is wrong — he was the last ruling Maharaja. Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad is wrong — he was a PM of J&K but is not known by this title.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lal Ded (Lalleshwari) is one of the most revered mystic poet-saints of Kashmir.
Reason (R): Her verses, known as 'Lal Vakhs', preach spiritual unity and transcend religious boundaries, making her respected by both Hindus and Muslims.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Lal Ded (14th century) is one of Kashmir's most revered mystic poets. Reason (R) is also correct — her verses (Lal Vakhs) preach universal spirituality beyond religious divisions. (R) explains (A) because it is her inclusive spiritual message that earned her veneration across religious communities in Kashmir. Option 2 is wrong because (R) gives the reason for her reverence. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following J&K personalities with their popular titles:

Column I:
(a) Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
(b) Habba Khatoon
(c) Ghulam Mohammad Sadiq
(d) Maharaja Ranbir Singh

Column II:
(i) Patron of Sanskrit and Dogri learning
(ii) Sher-e-Kashmir
(iii) Nightingale of Kashmir
(iv) Architect of Land Reforms in J&K

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah = Sher-e-Kashmir (Lion of Kashmir) — matches (ii). (b) Habba Khatoon = Nightingale of Kashmir — matches (iii). (c) Ghulam Mohammad Sadiq is known for implementing land reforms as CM of J&K — matches (iv). (d) Maharaja Ranbir Singh was a patron of Sanskrit learning and established educational institutions — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following personalities from J&K received the Param Vir Chakra?

(i) Major Somnath Sharma
(ii) Lance Naik Albert Ekka
(iii) Captain Vikram Batra
(iv) Havildar Abdul Hamid

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Major Somnath Sharma (from J&K) was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra for his bravery in the 1947 Kashmir operations. (iii) is correct — Captain Vikram Batra (though from Himachal Pradesh, he fought and was martyred in the Kargil sector of J&K) received the PVC posthumously in 1999. (ii) is wrong — Lance Naik Albert Ekka was from Jharkhand and fought in the 1971 Bangladesh war. (iv) is wrong — Havildar Abdul Hamid was from Uttar Pradesh and fought in the 1965 Indo-Pak war at Asal Uttar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Pandit Neh Kanth Ganjoo is known for his contribution to which field in J&K?
questions.explanation: Pandit Neh Kanth Ganjoo made significant contributions to Kashmiri literature and poetry. 'Political leadership' is wrong — he was primarily known in the literary field. 'Military service' is wrong — he was a literary figure, not a soldier. 'Scientific research' is wrong — his contributions were in the literary domain.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Agha Shahid Ali:

(i) He was a renowned Kashmiri-American poet.
(ii) He wrote in English and is known for his collection 'The Country Without a Post Office'.
(iii) He introduced the ghazal form into English poetry.
(iv) He was a politician from Srinagar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Agha Shahid Ali was born in New Delhi, grew up in Kashmir, and settled in the USA, becoming a celebrated poet. (ii) is correct — 'The Country Without a Post Office' (1997) is one of his most acclaimed collections about Kashmir. (iii) is correct — he championed and popularized the ghazal form in English (his anthology 'Ravishing Disunities'). (iv) is wrong — he was a poet and professor, not a politician.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: Zain-ul-Abidin, the 8th Sultan of Kashmir (1420–1470), is popularly known as __________.
questions.explanation: Zain-ul-Abidin is popularly called 'Budshah' (meaning 'The Great King') for his religious tolerance, patronage of arts, and development works. He is considered Kashmir's greatest ruler. 'Sher Shah' is wrong — that was Sher Shah Suri of the Delhi Sultanate. 'Akbar-e-Kashmir' is wrong — though his tolerance is compared to Akbar's, this is not his popular title. 'Sultan-e-Azam' is wrong — this generic title is not specifically associated with him.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Major Somnath Sharma is a celebrated hero of J&K.
Reason (R): He was the first recipient of India's highest wartime gallantry award, the Param Vir Chakra, for his bravery during the 1947 Kashmir operations.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Major Somnath Sharma is one of J&K's most honoured military heroes. Reason (R) is also correct — he received the first-ever PVC for leading his company against Pakistani raiders at Badgam on 3 November 1947, where he was killed in action. (R) explains (A) because his PVC-winning heroism is precisely why he is celebrated. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is the direct reason for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically verified. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who among the following is known as the 'Poet of the Common Man' in Kashmiri literature?
questions.explanation: Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor (1885–1952) is known as the 'Poet of the Common Man' (or People's Poet) for his Kashmiri poetry celebrating the lives of ordinary people and expressing their aspirations. Habba Khatoon is wrong — she is the Nightingale of Kashmir (love poetry). Lal Ded is wrong — she is a mystic saint-poet. Abdul Ahad Azad is wrong — he was a noted Kashmiri writer and historian but not specifically called the Poet of the Common Man.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following J&K personalities with their fields of achievement:

Column I:
(a) Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor
(b) Prem Nath Bazaz
(c) Maqbool Sherwani
(d) Karan Singh

Column II:
(i) Last Sadr-i-Riyasat / Scholar and Politician
(ii) Freedom fighter — resisted tribal raiders in 1947
(iii) Kashmiri poet (People's Poet)
(iv) Political journalist and writer

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor = Kashmiri People's Poet — matches (iii). (b) Prem Nath Bazaz = political journalist and author ('The History of Struggle for Freedom in Kashmir') — matches (iv). (c) Maqbool Sherwani = a young man of Baramulla who bravely misguided tribal raiders in 1947, delaying their advance toward Srinagar — matches (ii). (d) Karan Singh = son of Maharaja Hari Singh, last Sadr-i-Riyasat, scholar, diplomat — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which Kashmiri saint is credited with the introduction and spread of Islam in Kashmir in the 14th century?
questions.explanation: Mir Syed Ali Hamadani, known as Shah-e-Hamadan (King of Hamadan), is credited with the large-scale spread of Islam in Kashmir in the 14th century. He came from Hamadan (Iran) with hundreds of scholars. Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani is wrong — though a revered Kashmiri saint, he was a local mystic (Rishi order) who came after Hamadani. Bulbul Shah is wrong — he was the first Muslim missionary in Kashmir (early 14th century) but the large-scale spread is attributed to Hamadani. Zain-ul-Abidin is wrong — he was a tolerant king, not a religious missionary.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Karan Singh:

(i) He was the son of Maharaja Hari Singh.
(ii) He served as the last Sadr-i-Riyasat (Head of State) of J&K.
(iii) He was later appointed as India's Ambassador to the United States.
(iv) He was a military general in the Indian Army.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Karan Singh (born 1931) was the son and heir of Maharaja Hari Singh. (ii) is correct — he became the Regent (Yuvraj) and later the last Sadr-i-Riyasat of J&K (1952–1965). (iii) is correct — he served as India's Ambassador to the USA (and also as a Union Minister and Rajya Sabha member). (iv) is wrong — Karan Singh was a politician, diplomat, and scholar, not a military general.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly associated with J&K's literary heritage?

(i) Lal Ded — 14th century mystic poetess
(ii) Arnimal — 18th century romantic poetess
(iii) Rasul Mir — known as 'Keats of Kashmir'
(iv) Mahjoor — known as 'Wordsworth of Kashmir'

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Lal Ded (Lalleshwari) is the 14th-century mystic poetess whose Vakhs are foundational to Kashmiri literature. (ii) is correct — Arnimal (18th century) is known for her romantic lyrical poetry. (iii) is correct — Rasul Mir is called the 'Keats of Kashmiri poetry' for his romantic and lyrical verse. (iv) is correct — Mahjoor is sometimes compared to Wordsworth for his nature poetry and connection to common people. All four are correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah) is considered the greatest ruler of Kashmir.
Reason (R): He promoted religious tolerance, patronized arts, crafts, and learning, and built hospitals, bridges, and canals during his 50-year reign.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Budshah (r. 1420–1470) is widely regarded as Kashmir's greatest ruler. Reason (R) is also correct — he abolished the jizya tax, invited scholars, introduced paper-making, carpet-weaving, and built extensive infrastructure. (R) explains (A) because these achievements of tolerance and development are exactly what earned him the title 'Budshah' (Great King). Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides the reasons for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani is also known by which popular name?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani (1378–1438) is popularly known as Nund Rishi — he is the patron saint of Kashmir and founder of the Rishi order of Sufism in the valley. Shah-e-Hamadan is wrong — that is the title of Mir Syed Ali Hamadani. Bulbul Shah is wrong — he was a separate saint (early 14th century). Syed Ahmad is wrong — it is a generic name not associated with this saint.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The famous Kashmiri shawl is traditionally known as __________ and is famous worldwide for its intricate craftsmanship.
questions.explanation: Pashmina shawls are Kashmir's world-famous luxury product, made from fine cashmere wool of the Changthangi goat. 'Khadi' is wrong — it is hand-spun cotton/silk associated with the freedom movement. 'Chiffon' is wrong — it is a synthetic/silk fabric not specific to Kashmir. 'Muslin' is wrong — it is a cotton fabric historically associated with Bengal (Dhaka muslin).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Maqbool Sherwani:

(i) He was a young freedom fighter from Baramulla, Kashmir.
(ii) He misguided the Pakistani tribal raiders about the route to Srinagar in 1947.
(iii) His actions helped delay the raiders, giving the Indian Army time to land in Srinagar.
(iv) He was a military officer in the Indian Army.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Maqbool Sherwani was a young man (19 years old) from Baramulla. (ii) is correct — he deliberately misguided the tribal invaders about directions, delaying their march. (iii) is correct — his delay helped buy crucial time for Indian forces to be airlifted to Srinagar on 27 October 1947. (iv) is wrong — Sherwani was a civilian volunteer of the National Conference, not a military officer; he was captured and killed by the raiders.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who was the first Chief Minister of Jammu & Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah served as the first Prime Minister (equivalent to CM) of J&K from 1948 to 1953 (the post was called 'Prime Minister' at that time). Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad is wrong — he succeeded Sheikh Abdullah as PM in 1953. Ghulam Mohammad Sadiq is wrong — he became CM in 1964 (the title was changed from PM to CM). Mir Qasim is wrong — he served as CM from 1971 to 1975.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Gulab Singh is considered the founder of the Dogra dynasty in Jammu & Kashmir.
Reason (R): He acquired the territory of Kashmir through the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) with the British.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Gulab Singh established the Dogra dynasty's rule over J&K. Reason (R) is also correct — the Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846) transferred Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh rupees after the Anglo-Sikh War. (R) explains (A) because this treaty is the specific event that made Gulab Singh the ruler and founder of the Dogra kingdom of J&K. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is the mechanism by which (A) happened. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically documented. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following personalities with their contributions to J&K:

Column I:
(a) Mir Syed Ali Hamadani
(b) Lal Ded
(c) Zain-ul-Abidin
(d) Arnimal

Column II:
(i) Romantic poetry in Kashmiri
(ii) Spread of Islam and handicrafts in Kashmir
(iii) Spiritual verses (Vakhs) transcending religion
(iv) Patronage of arts, religious harmony, and development

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Mir Syed Ali Hamadani spread Islam and introduced handicrafts (carpet-weaving, paper-making) — matches (ii). (b) Lal Ded composed Vakhs (spiritual verses) accepted across religious lines — matches (iii). (c) Zain-ul-Abidin patronized arts, promoted religious harmony, and undertook development — matches (iv). (d) Arnimal was known for her romantic Kashmiri poetry — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Pt. Dina Nath Nadim is known for his contribution to:
questions.explanation: Pt. Dina Nath Nadim (1916–1988) was a pioneer of modern Kashmiri literature, known for his plays (especially 'Shuhul Kaul') and progressive poetry. 'Military strategy' is wrong — he was a literary figure. 'Architectural design' is wrong — his contributions were purely literary. 'Scientific invention' is wrong — he was a poet and dramatist.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched?

(i) Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor — Kashmiri poet honoured with title 'People's Poet'
(ii) Abdul Ahad Azad — historian and author of 'Kashmiri Zuban aur Shairi'
(iii) Zinda Kaul 'Masterji' — Kashmiri poet and educationist
(iv) Somnath Sharma — literary figure and novelist

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Mahjoor is called the People's Poet for his Kashmiri poetry celebrating common folk. (ii) is correct — Abdul Ahad Azad was a Kashmiri literary historian and writer. (iii) is correct — Zinda Kaul 'Masterji' was a revered Kashmiri poet and teacher. (iv) is wrong — Major Somnath Sharma was a military hero (first PVC recipient), NOT a literary figure.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who is known as 'Bulbul Shah' and what was his significance?
options: A Sufi saint — the first Muslim missionary to arrive in Kashmir
A Kashmiri singer — famous for folk music
A poet — wrote in Persian about Kashmir
questions.correctAnswer: A Sufi saint — the first Muslim missionary to arrive in Kashmir
questions.explanation: Bulbul Shah (Syed Sharafuddin Abdur Rahman) was a Sufi saint from Turkestan who is considered the first Muslim missionary to arrive in Kashmir (early 14th century). He converted the Buddhist ruler Rinchana to Islam. 'A singer' is wrong — Bulbul Shah was a Sufi saint, not a musician. 'A Dogra general' is wrong — he lived centuries before the Dogra period. 'A poet in Persian' is wrong — he was a missionary and saint, not primarily a poet.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad:

(i) He succeeded Sheikh Abdullah as Prime Minister of J&K in 1953.
(ii) He is known for major developmental works including roads, schools, and housing.
(iii) He served as a judge of the High Court.
(iv) He was associated with the National Conference party.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad became PM of J&K on 9 August 1953 after Sheikh Abdullah's dismissal. (ii) is correct — he undertook extensive development: the Bakshi Stadium, housing colonies, road construction, and educational expansion. (iv) is correct — he was a senior leader of the Jammu & Kashmir National Conference. (iii) is wrong — he was a political leader and administrator, not a judge.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which ancient ruler of Kashmir is famous for writing the historical chronicle 'Rajatarangini' about his reign?
options: The Rajatarangini was written by Kalhana, a historian, not a ruler
questions.correctAnswer: The Rajatarangini was written by Kalhana, a historian, not a ruler
questions.explanation: 'Rajatarangini' (River of Kings) was written by the historian Kalhana in the 12th century (1148–1150 AD), not by any ruler. It is a chronicle of Kashmir's kings. Lalitaditya Muktapida is wrong — he was a powerful 8th-century ruler but didn't write Rajatarangini. Avantivarman is wrong — he was a 9th-century king who built irrigation works. Didda is wrong — she was a powerful 10th–11th century queen-regent.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lalitaditya Muktapida is considered one of the greatest rulers of ancient Kashmir.
Reason (R): He expanded his kingdom far beyond Kashmir's borders through military conquests and was a great patron of art and architecture, including the famous Martand Sun Temple.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Lalitaditya Muktapida (r. 724–760 AD) of the Karkota dynasty is celebrated as one of Kashmir's greatest kings. Reason (R) is also correct — he defeated many kingdoms and built the magnificent Martand Sun Temple at Anantnag. (R) explains (A) because his military achievements and architectural legacy are the reasons he is considered great. Option 2 is wrong because (R) gives specific reasons for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who among the following was the first woman ruler of Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Queen Didda (r. 980–1003 AD) was the first notable woman ruler of Kashmir who wielded supreme power as regent and then as sovereign. Habba Khatoon is wrong — she was a poetess and queen consort, not a ruling sovereign. Kota Rani is wrong — she was the last Hindu queen of Kashmir (14th century) but came after Didda. Lal Ded is wrong — she was a mystic poet-saint, not a ruler.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following J&K personalities are associated with the Dogra period?

(i) Gulab Singh
(ii) Ranbir Singh
(iii) Pratap Singh
(iv) Hari Singh

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Gulab Singh (r. 1846–1857) — founder of the Dogra kingdom ✓. (ii) Ranbir Singh (r. 1857–1885) — son of Gulab Singh, patron of learning ✓. (iii) Pratap Singh (r. 1885–1925) — known for reforms and the Gilgit Agency ✓. (iv) Hari Singh (r. 1925–1947) — last ruling Maharaja who signed the Instrument of Accession ✓. All four were Dogra rulers.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Kota Rani was the last Hindu ruler of Kashmir. She belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Kota Rani (d. 1339) was the last Hindu ruler of Kashmir, belonging to the later Lohara dynasty. After her death, Shah Mir established Muslim rule. Karkota dynasty is wrong — that was the dynasty of Lalitaditya (8th century). Utpala dynasty is wrong — that came between the Karkota and Lohara periods. Dogra dynasty is wrong — Dogra rule began much later in 1846.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Rishi order of Sufism in Kashmir:

(i) It was founded by Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani (Nund Rishi).
(ii) The Rishi saints were vegetarian and lived simple, ascetic lives.
(iii) The Rishi order blended Islamic Sufism with local Shaivite traditions.
(iv) The Rishi order was introduced by Mir Syed Ali Hamadani from Iran.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Nund Rishi (1378–1438) founded the indigenous Rishi order of Sufism. (ii) is correct — Rishi saints practiced vegetarianism, meditation, and lived in caves or forests. (iii) is correct — the Rishi order uniquely combined Islamic mysticism with elements of Kashmir's indigenous spiritual traditions. (iv) is wrong — Shah-e-Hamadan introduced the Kubrawi order from Iran; the Rishi order was an indigenous Kashmiri creation by Nund Rishi.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following J&K rulers with their notable achievements:

Column I:
(a) Lalitaditya Muktapida
(b) Avantivarman
(c) Zain-ul-Abidin
(d) Didda

Column II:
(i) Irrigation canals built by his engineer Suyya
(ii) Military conquests and Martand Sun Temple
(iii) Religious tolerance and revival of crafts
(iv) First notable woman sovereign of Kashmir

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Lalitaditya built the Martand Sun Temple and expanded the kingdom through conquests — matches (ii). (b) Avantivarman's engineer Suyya cleared Jhelum river channels and built irrigation — matches (i). (c) Zain-ul-Abidin promoted religious tolerance and revived Kashmir's crafts — matches (iii). (d) Didda was the first major woman sovereign — matches (iv). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who is credited with establishing the first modern educational institution in J&K?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Ranbir Singh (r. 1857–1885) is credited with promoting modern education in J&K, establishing schools and the Sri Ranbir Sanskrit Research Library. He also patronized translation of Sanskrit texts. Gulab Singh is wrong — he focused on consolidating his rule rather than modern education. Hari Singh is wrong — though he continued educational development, Ranbir Singh pioneered it. Sheikh Abdullah is wrong — his educational contributions came in the 20th century.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the contribution of Kashmiri Pandits to learning:

(i) Kalhana wrote 'Rajatarangini', a historical chronicle of Kashmir.
(ii) Abhinavagupta was a renowned philosopher of Kashmir Shaivism.
(iii) Pandit Anand Kaul was a noted historian of modern Kashmir.
(iv) All Kashmiri Pandits were rulers of Kashmir.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Kalhana composed Rajatarangini in Sanskrit (1148–50 AD), chronicling Kashmir's kings. (ii) is correct — Abhinavagupta (10th–11th century) was a master philosopher of the Kashmir Shaiva school. (iii) is correct — Pandit Anand Kaul wrote extensively on Kashmir's history, culture, and geography in the early 20th century. (iv) is wrong — Kashmiri Pandits were scholars, priests, administrators, and professionals, NOT rulers (rulers belonged to various dynasties).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Dogri' language is primarily associated with which region of J&K?
questions.explanation: Dogri is the mother tongue of the Dogra people, spoken primarily in the Jammu region. It was recognized as a scheduled language under the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution in 2003. 'Kashmir Valley' is wrong — the Kashmir Valley primarily speaks Kashmiri. 'Ladakh' is wrong — Ladakh primarily uses Ladakhi/Bhoti. 'Kargil' is wrong — Kargil primarily uses Balti and Purgi.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs of personalities and their contributions are correctly matched?

(i) Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru — ancestral roots in Kashmir
(ii) Allama Iqbal — wrote 'Saare Jahan Se Accha'
(iii) Both Nehru and Iqbal had connections to Kashmir
(iv) Allama Iqbal was born in Srinagar

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Nehru family (Kashmiri Pandits) had ancestral roots in Kashmir. (ii) is correct — Allama Iqbal wrote 'Saare Jahan Se Accha Hindustan Hamara'. (iii) is correct — both had Kashmiri connections: Nehru ancestrally, and Iqbal through his Kashmiri Brahmin ancestry (the Sapru family that converted to Islam). (iv) is wrong — Allama Iqbal was born in Sialkot (now in Pakistan), not Srinagar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Who is known as 'Alamdar-e-Kashmir' (Flag Bearer of Kashmir)?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah earned the title 'Alamdar-e-Kashmir' in addition to 'Sher-e-Kashmir', reflecting his role as the leading political figure and voice of the Kashmiri people's aspirations. Mir Waiz Yusuf Shah is wrong — though a religious leader, this specific title belongs to Sheikh Abdullah. Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad is wrong — he was a political leader but not known by this title. Ghulam Mohammad Sadiq is wrong — he was a CM but not associated with this title.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about crafts associated with J&K:

(i) Pashmina shawl weaving is a traditional craft of Kashmir.
(ii) Papier-mâché craft was introduced during the time of Zain-ul-Abidin.
(iii) The walnut wood carving is a traditional craft of Kashmir.
(iv) Carpet weaving in Kashmir was introduced by Shah-e-Hamadan.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Pashmina shawl weaving has been practiced in Kashmir for centuries. (ii) is correct — papier-mâché craft flourished under Zain-ul-Abidin's patronage. (iii) is correct — walnut wood carving is a renowned traditional Kashmiri craft. (iv) is correct — Shah-e-Hamadan (Mir Syed Ali Hamadani) is credited with introducing carpet weaving to Kashmir in the 14th century. All four are correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Pratap Singh (Maharaja of J&K, 1885–1925) is notably remembered for:
options: Administrative reforms and establishing the Gilgit Agency
questions.correctAnswer: Administrative reforms and establishing the Gilgit Agency
questions.explanation: Maharaja Pratap Singh implemented administrative reforms during his long reign and the Gilgit Agency was established during his period. He also patronized education and infrastructure. 'Building Martand Sun Temple' is wrong — that was Lalitaditya (8th century). 'Introducing Islam' is wrong — Islam came to Kashmir centuries earlier. 'Writing Rajatarangini' is wrong — that was Kalhana (12th century).
